change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The change extends the brake override priority to apply even when a diagnostic fault is active. This means that in fault conditions, the emergency brake command must still take precedence over positive propulsion torque. Verification must now include scenarios where a diagnostic fault is active during brake override tests.

assessments.reason: The test verifies driver torque response timing under VCU-DR-01, which is not modified by the change to VCU-BRK-03.
evidence: Test verifies torque response time (94 ms) against VCU-DR-01, which is unchanged.
No interaction with brake override logic is tested.

assessments.reason: The test verifies brake override priority, which is directly modified by the addition of the diagnostic fault condition in VCU-BRK-03. The existing procedure does not include an active diagnostic fault, so the previous evidence does not cover the new requirement.
evidence: Test is linked to VCU-BRK-03.
Procedure applies emergency brake with 85% pedal but does not mention active diagnostic faults.
Previous result was PASS but did not cover the new fault condition.
assessments.recommended_action: Update the test procedure to include an active diagnostic fault scenario and rerun.
